subject: Unable to add bank details — duplicate Zip entity records blocking bank link
messages:
From: Danielle Hart <danielle.hart@ceruleanmfg.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@ceruleanmfg.com
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Trouble linking bank account after accepting Zip invite

Hi Laura —

We accepted the invite to Redwood's supplier portal (Zip) this morning but when I try to add our bank details I get an error: "Duplicate vendor record detected — choose the entity to claim". The system shows two records for our company ("Cerulean Manufacturing - US" and "Cerulean Mfg - HQ") with different internal IDs. Both look incomplete and neither lets me add ACH details. I attached a screenshot of the UI state.

We need this set up before the PO on Friday. Happy to share any docs you need (W-9, bank letter, DUNS). Please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Danielle Hart
Director, Finance
Cerulean Manufacturing
(danielle.hart@ceruleanmfg.com)

Attachments: duplicate_entity_screenshot.png
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Danielle Hart <danielle.hart@ceruleanmfg.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble linking bank account after accepting Zip invite

Thanks for the note, Danielle — looping in Ben (procurement) and Monica (platform ops).

Ben / Monica: vendor is stuck on bank link due to duplicate entity records in Zip. Vendor reports two records (different internal IDs). Can ops confirm whether the duplicates came from a previous CSV import vs. an earlier invite?

Danielle — can you confirm the DUNS and the EIN you used when claiming the account? If you can send the W-9 and a bank letter that will speed manual reconciliation. Monica, please advise if we can do a backend merge or if Zip requires vendor-led claim selection.

Laura Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Danielle Hart <danielle.hart@ceruleanmfg.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble linking bank account after accepting Zip invite

Quick triage notes:
- Risk: if we pick the wrong canonical entity and payments are routed to a stale profile, ACH will bounce.
- Root cause hypothesis: earlier procurement CSV import (2019) created a legacy profile that wasn't fully merged when Cerulean accepted the new invite.

Monica - can your team pull the two Zip record IDs and check DUNS/EIN fields? If the legacy record lacks bank info, we can either (A) request vendor to claim the preferred record via a secure claim link, or (B) perform a controlled merge on our side if Zip supports a server-side merge with vendor consent. Option B is faster if we have the W-9 + bank letter.

I'm attaching our vendor-relationship-mapping.csv that maps the different site IDs for Cerulean across systems.

Ben Carter
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vendor-relationship-mapping.csv
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Danielle Hart <danielle.hart@ceruleanmfg.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble linking bank account after accepting Zip invite

Hi Danielle — thanks for the screenshot, that helped. I pulled the two records: Zip IDs ZP-48321 (legacy) and ZP-201947 (new claim). DUNS are present on both but only the new claim has a company address that matches your W-9.

We can do a server-side merge but Zip requires written vendor consent for merging PII and bank data. To avoid back-and-forth, we can send you a secure one-time claim link (valid 48 hours) that will let you choose the canonical record and then re-run the bank-link flow. Steps:
1) Reply with the best DUNS/EIN you prefer we use (or attach W-9).
2) We'll generate a secure claim link and send it to your accounts-payable inbox.
3) After you claim, attempt bank link again and copy us if you see an error.

If you prefer, we can open support ticket with Zip to perform a merge on your behalf (they will still ask for the W-9). Which would you prefer?

Monica Patel
Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Danielle Hart <danielle.hart@ceruleanmfg.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@ceruleanmfg.com
Date: 2026-11-21T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Trouble linking bank account after accepting Zip invite

Monica — thanks, we can do either. To move fast, please send the secure claim link and we'll accept it and try the bank flow. I'm attaching a signed W-9 and a bank confirmation letter (PDFs). If Zip still blocks the ACH, we'll authorize Redwood to proceed with a merge.

Attaching: w9_cerulean_2026.pdf

—
Danielle Hart
Director, Finance
Cerulean Manufacturing
